entry.title: LiveMACE: Process-Aware Evaluation of LLM Agent Capabilities in Evolving Markets
entry.summary:
Evaluating agents by outcomes alone can obscure the capabilities that produce them. This problem is especially pronounced in evolving environments, where outcomes reflect a closed-loop interaction between agent behavior and changing external conditions. We introduce LiveMACEBench, a process-aware benchmark that uses live financial markets as a naturally evolving testbed for persistent LLM agents.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: Scene-Designer: Learning Design Intelligence for Agentic 3D Scene Generation
entry.summary:
Generating complete, coherent, and usable 3D indoor scenes from natural language requires strong design intelligence: the ability to design high-quality scenes and critique their quality. However, existing approaches either rely on general-purpose models lacking domain-specific design experience or learn from static scenes. In this work, we introduce Scene-Designer, an agentic framework that learns design intelligence through complementary design and critique experiences.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: BridgeWAM: Bridging Video and Action Experts via Latent Bridge Queries
entry.summary:
World Action Models (WAMs) commonly couple video and action experts through dense, layer-wise Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention, exposing action prediction to irrelevant visual features while enforcing matched expert depths. This coupling hinders selective visual-feature use and introduces redundant computation. We introduce Bridge-of-Experts (BoE), instantiated as BridgeWAM, which aggregates visual, language, and proprioceptive priors through 32 Latent Bridge Queries (LBQs) into a shared, limited latent space.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #robotics

entry.title: Learning to Think and Explore in 3D World. We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space.
entry.summary:
We study how vision-language models (VLMs) can learn to think and actively explore in 3D space. Instead of providing multi-view images, videos, or 3D representations to the model, we preserve the native visual encoding of VLMs, i.e., a single image, one at a time, just like humans, and treat the 3D representation only as an environment with which the model can interact through actions (e.g., move left) and observations (rendered images). Each rollout begins from an initial first-person view and a visual question.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #reinforcement-learning

entry.title: Lexical Reference Frames: Interpreting LM Residual Streams in Native Semantics
entry.summary:
The vocabulary of a language model is its native semantics: the embedding and the unembedding fix the meaning of a state at the two ends of the residual stream. Between them, existing methods either reuse a fixed lens or treat the states as a point cloud, and neither reads a state the way the model does. We argue that every hidden state has a native reference frame, induced by the layers that read it next and adaptive to the context.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights

entry.title: RAP: A Dataset for Paper-to-Poster Generation via Declarative Markup from Human-Crafted Exemplars
entry.summary:
Making a conference poster is visual coding in miniature: an entire paper must be compressed onto a single page, which exercises summarization, visual design, and code implementation at once, using nothing beyond the paper itself. Yet benchmarks for this task in the context of visual coding remain scarce: existing resources are small and annotated only with layout boxes, so evaluation must fall back on VLM-as-judge or human checklists rather than objective render-and-compare, and the generation methods they support design layouts from scratch, leaving human-crafted posters unusable as either a retrievable design library or as verified supervision. We introduce RAP (Reconstruct A Poster), a dataset and benchmark for paper-to-poster generation as a visual coding task.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #open-weights #agents

entry.title: Can Visual Generation Expand What Unified Multimodal Models Know?. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) receive image-generation supervision that exposes them to visual information not fully documented in text.
entry.summary:
Unified multimodal models (UMMs) receive image-generation supervision that exposes them to visual information not fully documented in text. Can learning to generate images expand what pretrained models know? We introduce Knowledge Transfer Probing (KTP), a controlled protocol that supplies new knowledge through image-generation training and tests its accessibility through text-only question answering.

entry.title: Doom GPU Flame Graphs
entry.summary:
Imagine halving the resource costs of AI and what that could mean for the planet and the industry -- based on extreme estimates such savings could reduce the total US power usage by over 10% by 2030 1 . At Intel we've been creating a new analyzer tool to help reduce AI costs called AI Flame Graphs : a visualization that shows an AI accelerator or GPU hardware profile along with the full software stack, based on my CPU flame graphs . Our first version is available to customers in the Intel Tiber AI Cloud as a preview for the Intel Data Center GPU Max Series (previously called Ponte Vecchio).

Source: Brendan Gregg (Systems Performance & eBPF) · Tags: #kernel-os #performance #compilers #combinatorics

entry.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
entry.summary:
We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #algebra-geometry #high-energy

entry.title: The semiring of spectral duality skeletons: cancellation, characters and factorization
entry.summary:
Weighted dual skeletons are the combinatorial core of spectral duality structures. Their isomorphism classes, under Cartesian product and disjoint union, form a semiring graded by the degree. We identify it completely: a class is determined by its degree, a symmetric element of the group semiring N_0[R] and its number of fixed points.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #algebra-geometry #probability-stats

entry.title: Market Efficiency in a Changing Asset Population: Mobility, Entry, and Survival over Cryptocurrency's Full History
entry.summary:
Weak-form efficiency implies symmetry restrictions on the Markov chain governing movement across the cryptocurrency capitalisation distribution. We test them on the full listed population: 8,970 assets, 690 weekly cross-sections, 2013 to 2026, with entry, exit and survival observed rather than inferred. Symmetry is rejected in every era, but the asymmetry falls by seventy percent, and what converged is entry-driven compositional churn rather than coins' own valuations.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance

entry.title: Proportionality in Ranking Compression
entry.summary:
Motivated by applications in reinforcement learning from human feedback, we consider a setting where a given collection of rankings needs to be compressed into a smaller collection of rankings. This can also be seen as a combination of two fundamental social choice frameworks: ranking aggregation and multiwinner voting. We propose three proportionality notions that capture different types of representation in this setting: positional proportionality, pairwise proportionality, and proportionality for solid coalitions (PSC).

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #ml-theory

entry.title: The Source of Data Value: Consumer Disclosure, Access Design, and Platform Monetization
entry.summary:
Digital marketplaces increasingly earn revenue from transaction commissions and seller-facing data services. Sellers may purchase data to increase revenue or avoid competing with an informed rival. We examine how consumer disclosure rights shape these motives and the platform's incentive to provide data.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #optimization

entry.title: Agentic AI in Automated Markets. Automated markets increasingly host autonomous, learning trading agents and are powered by formulaic automated market makers (AMMs).
entry.summary:
Automated markets increasingly host autonomous, learning trading agents and are powered by formulaic automated market makers (AMMs). We study how heterogeneous agent behavior shapes stress, risk-adjusted performance, liquidity, and volatility in these types of markets. Three behavioral archetypes are modeled as agentic reinforcement learning (RL) systems: a rational arbitrageur, a manipulator, and a retail herd-follower.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #quant-finance #agents

entry.title: Bypassing Administrator Protection by Abusing UI Access. A headline feature introduced in the latest release of Windows 11, 25H2 is Administrator Protection.
entry.summary:
A headline feature introduced in the latest release of Windows 11, 25H2 is Administrator Protection. The goal of this feature is to replace User Account Control (UAC) with a more robust and importantly, securable system to allow a local user to access administrator privileges only when necessary. This blog post will give a brief overview of the new feature, how it works and how it’s different from UAC.

Source: Google Project Zero · Tags: #infosec #kernel-os

entry.title: Anyonic Neural Network Wavefunctions. The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades.
entry.summary:
The macroscopic behavior of a non-interacting gas of Abelian anyons has remained unsettled for many decades. Prior numerical methods employing exact diagonalization in the continuum and on the plane have been limited to small system sizes, at most $N = 4$ anyons. Using the rapidly developing technology of neural network wavefunctions, we develop variational ansatze appropriate for studying continuum models of the Abelian anyon gas.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #high-energy #neuroscience

entry.title: Orbital Angular Momentum Currents and Textures in a Multiorbital Double Helix
entry.summary:
The microscopic origin of chirality induced spin selectivity (CISS) in biomolecular structures has traditionally been discussed in terms of spin orbit coupling and spin angular momentum. However, orbital angular momentum (OAM) is increasingly recognized as a more direct electronic response to molecular chirality. A helical hopping network built only from s orbitals can support an itinerant orbital moment and an orbital Edelstein response, but such a basis has no local atomic OAM and therefore omits the complementary contribution arising from coherence among active p orbitals.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
entry.summary:
Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #semiconductors

entry.title: Temperature and Thickness Dependent Spin Current Transmission through Epitaxial Antiferromagnetic α-Fe2O3
entry.summary:
Antiferromagnetic insulator α-Fe2O3 is a potential medium for coherent motion of spin waves over relatively large distances, allowing non-dissipative transfer of information between circuit elements. However, the structural defects and temperature dependent spin reorientations in this oxide impact the propagation. Understanding how the magnetic state of an antiferromagnetic insulator affects spin-current transmission is therefore important for elucidating the mechanisms governing spin transport.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science

entry.title: Limits from nonlinear loss of spin-orbit-torque control of magnon transport
entry.summary:
Controlling magnon currents is central to the development of magnonic devices, which exploit spin excitations for information transport without charge flow. Here, we use the spin-orbit torque (SOT) from a Pt gate to control the effective magnon damping in three-terminal devices fabricated from low-damping lithium aluminum ferrite (LAFO) thin films and identify the nonlinear damping that ultimately limits the gate response. With increasing gate current, the nonlocal magnon signal initially increases, but saturates and subsequently decreases above a critical gate current density.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #materials-science #infosec

entry.title: Holographic two-point functions across a PT symmetry-breaking transition
entry.summary:
In parity-time (PT)-symmetric non-Hermitian systems, an exceptional point, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors coalesce, typically separates a real spectrum from complex-conjugate eigenvalues. In logarithmic conformal field theories (LCFTs), such an exceptional point appears in the spectrum of scaling dimensions. Holographic models of LCFTs, such as the dipole model, are built exactly at this point.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #high-energy #combinatorics

entry.title: Renormalization Group Domain Walls from Phantom Symmetries. We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories.
entry.summary:
We develop a systematic construction of renormalization group (RG) domain walls between two-dimensional rational conformal field theories. Using phantom currents, we consider an auxiliary chiral extension linked to the folded ultraviolet--infrared theory by a topological interface. The construction of RG walls then reduces to identifying suitable automorphism-twisted Cardy states in the auxiliary theory.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #high-energy #topology

entry.title: ConQUESTA: Topology-Aware Post-Training Structural Pruning of Quantum Neural Networks
entry.summary:
Deploying quantum neural networks (QNNs) on sparse hardware requires preserving task accuracy while reducing compiler-induced two-qubit gates, SWAPs, and depth. We present ConQUESTA (\underline{C}onstrained \underline{Qu}antum \underline{E}ntangler \underline{S}election with \underline{T}opology \underline{A}wareness), a post training pruning framework that combines task saliency with compiler cost, screens candidate entanglers, and searches complete pruning masks under an explicit accuracy constraint. Unlike one-shot ranking, each mask is transpiled as a whole across multiple coupling topologies.

Source: arXiv Quantum & Condensed Matter (quant-ph, cond-mat) · Tags: #quantum-computing #condensed-matter #computer-architecture #compilers

entry.title: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
entry.summary:
Classical execution models assume linear impact, diffusive prices, and an exogenous horizon. We study execution under concave power-law impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations, and make two contributions. First, we choose the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #quant-finance #optimization

entry.title: Recursive Operator Localization and Spectral Gap Descent via the Geometry of Local Spectral Expansion
entry.summary:
We introduce Recursive Operator Localization (ROL), a framework for constructing hierarchies of local energy problems linked by linear maps between Hilbert spaces. To address spectral-gap problems, including those arising in quantum systems, we study a realization of ROL by nested subspaces indexed by a weighted simplicial complex. Using spectral gaps of auxiliary classical random walks on links, we propagate geometric estimates upward and use them to turn local spectral gaps at the bottom of the hierarchy into a spectral-gap bound for the global operator.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #quantum-computing

entry.title: The Covering Radius of $\text{RM}(1,9)$ is Precisely $242$
entry.summary:
Let $\text{RM}(r,n)$ be the $r$th order Reed-Muller code of length $2^n$, and let $\rho(r,n)$ denote its covering radius, so that $\rho(1,n)$ is the largest possible nonlinearity of a Boolean function in $n$ variables. For odd $n$, the value of $\rho(1,n)$ was previously known only for $n\le 7$. It is known that $242\le\rho(1,9)\le 244$, but the exact determination of $\rho(1,9)$ has been a long-standing open question.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp
